best.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
best.label: Receptions
best.why: In Daniels' first start, Godwin was his safety valve with six catches on seven targets, and Tampa should again rely on short throws while trailing by more than a touchdown. Dallas allows the league's worst success rate on dropbacks, and Godwin has gone over this line in six of his last 10 games.

best.name: Brock Purdy
best.label: Rushing yards
best.why: Purdy has run for 29 to 34 yards in all four games this season, and Seattle has already allowed 40-plus rushing yards to mobile quarterbacks while its tight coverage tends to force scrambles. Kalshi prices the over near 50%, below the 52.4% break-even, for a number he has cleared every week.

best.name: Matthew Stafford
best.label: Passing yards
best.why: Stafford has passed for 300 or more yards in three straight games, and Buffalo's pass defense is short-handed with DT Ed Oliver out and nickel Dee Alford questionable. The game is indoors with a total that rose to about 54.5, and a prediction market prices 275+ yards slightly above even.

best.name: Bryce Young
best.label: Passing yards
best.why: Bryce Young has thrown for 280+ yards in all four of his starts (about 317 per game, the league lead) and Carolina's offense runs through his arm. Jalen Coker is back at full practice, and the posted line (now 249.5 at consensus) still sits well under his weekly floor.

best.name: Jayden Daniels
best.label: Rush attempts
best.why: Lead back Jacory Croskey-Merritt is ruled out after missing every practice, leaving a White-Ekeler split with both limited this week. Daniels practiced fully and ran 9 times in his return last week, so 7+ carries needs only his normal designed-run and scramble load.

best.name: Josh Hart
best.label: Rebounds
best.why: Josh Hart is probable after full practice Monday, with the ankle soreness costing him only the preseason finale. Mitchell Robinson's move to Boston and Philadelphia's thin frontcourt leave more defensive rebounds for him; the stats lean over and the line has held at 7.5 with the book slightly favoring the over.

best.name: D'Andre Swift
best.label: Rush attempts
best.why: Monangai is ruled out for a third straight game, and Swift has handled 16 and 20 carries as the lead back in that stretch. Chicago is a short home favorite that leans on the run, and previews favor his attempts over his yardage because his efficiency has been uneven. Roschon Johnson's share is the main risk.

best.name: Bijan Robinson
best.label: Rush + Rec yards
best.why: Brian Robinson (hamstring) is out and only practice-squad elevation Khalil Herbert backs Bijan up, so his touch share should be near total. San Francisco has ruled out Nick Bosa and two linebackers, and the game is in a dome. Books post 120.5 to 124.5, below the app's 125.5, so the over is easier at the posted number.
